primary_source.title: Stop Guessing When to Stop Testing: Efficient Model Evaluation with Just Enough Data

claim_checks.claim: The experiments use 206 VLMs across 31 multimodal benchmarks from the Open VLM Leaderboard.
claim_checks.primary_location: ACL PDF p.875, section 6.1; extracted PDF lines 386-401
claim_checks.detail: The paper states 206 VLMs evaluated across 31 multimodal benchmarks and uses an unweighted mean-of-means. Released records contain predictions; the study uses the leaderboard LLM-as-a-Judge implementation with Llama 3.1 8B to extract scores.

claim_checks.claim: The method uses group-sequential testing with Pocock spending / adjusted interim significance to avoid invalid repeated peeking.
claim_checks.primary_location: ACL PDF p.874, sections 5.1-5.2; extracted PDF lines 257-340
claim_checks.detail: The paper explicitly formalizes group sequential testing with the Pocock spending function, stage-adjusted significance thresholds and adjusted CIs; Pocock controls overall Type-I error across repeated looks.

claim_checks.claim: About 15%, 30%, and 50% of samples suffice for ±3, ±2, and ±1.5 point confidence targets.
claim_checks.primary_location: ACL PDF p.876, section 7.1; extracted PDF lines 455-475
claim_checks.detail: The paper explicitly defines the plotted quantity as 95% CI half-width and reports ≈15% for ±3, ~30% for ±2, and about half for ±1.5. Downstream wording should say CI half-width/margin (or ± target), not unqualified 'CI width', because full interval width would be twice these values.

claim_checks.claim: At 8K/14.4K examples the CI measure is 2.9 vs 2.7 points, showing diminishing returns.
claim_checks.primary_location: ACL PDF p.876, section 7.1; extracted PDF lines 470-480
claim_checks.detail: The paper says 8K examples (55%) gives CI width 2.9 and full 14,400 gives 2.7, a 0.2-point difference. This sentence uses 'width' while the surrounding experiment discusses half-width/± thresholds; preserve the paper's exact wording rather than silently normalizing these two terms.

claim_checks.claim: For >2-point pairwise gaps the framework usually saves at least 60% of evaluation effort; a fixed 1.2K heuristic distinguishes 55% of 1K pairs vs 76% for the sequential framework.
claim_checks.primary_location: ACL PDF pp.877-878, section 7.2; extracted PDF lines 540-570; visual inspection of p.877-878
claim_checks.detail: The paper states >2-point gaps usually save at least 60%. The fixed baseline uses 200 examples per dataset, 1.2K total, with bootstrapping; only 55% of 1K pairs are differentiated at 95% confidence vs 76% with the adaptive framework.

claim_checks.claim: A practical ≥2-point improvement/futility deployment case averages ~63% of examples.
claim_checks.primary_location: ACL PDF p.878, section 7.3.2; extracted PDF lines 590-607; visual inspection of p.878
claim_checks.detail: Across 100 randomly sampled top-15 pairs, the one-sided stopping rule requires a ≥2-point improvement with 95% confidence or stops when such improvement is deemed unlikely; average sample use is 63% of the fixed-sample approach.

statistical_assumptions: approximately normal group-sequential test statistic under the null
pre-specified number of stages for the demonstrated method
scope_and_limitations.experiment_defaults: initial sample size 600 (100/model), batch size 100 per iteration, beta 0.9, Pocock spending; defaults were not tuned
scope_and_limitations.multiple_model_warning: The paper explicitly says pairwise comparisons among multiple models introduce multiple-hypothesis-testing corrections and that this aspect is simplified for the study. Therefore the reported pairwise guarantees must not be broadened into a fully family-wise-error-controlled many-model ranking guarantee.
scope_and_limitations.data_dependence_warning: The demonstrated experiments are sample-level VLM benchmark evaluations; the paper itself notes i.i.d. assumptions may fail in practice. This is not direct validation for clustered/dependent long-horizon agent trajectories.
scope_and_limitations.reproducibility_warning: Stopping points vary with observed performance and can vary across runs unless randomness is tightly controlled.
scope_and_limitations.decision_threshold_warning: Equivalence margins/performance gaps are user/domain choices; the paper does not provide a universal optimal margin.

downstream_correction.target: research_index_clean_g1/O_FEED.json and evidence comparator wording for this source-qualified candidate
downstream_correction.change: Replace ambiguous '±3/±2/±1.5pp widths' wording with '95% CI half-width targets of ±3/±2/±1.5pp' (or equivalent). Keep the many-model multiple-comparison limitation explicit if applying this beyond pairwise comparisons.
downstream_correction.candidate_family_effect: none; this is a terminology/scope clarification, not negative evidence against sequential evaluation
